sn47.21:1.2: On one occasion the Venerable Ānanda and the Venerable Bhadda were dwelling at Paṭaliputta in the Cock’s Park.
sn47.21:1.3: Then, in the evening, the Venerable Bhadda emerged from seclusion, approached the Venerable Ānanda, and exchanged greetings with him.
sn47.21:1.4: When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side and said to the Venerable Ānanda:
sn47.21:1.5: “Friend Ānanda, as to the wholesome virtues spoken of by the Blessed One, what is the purpose for which they were spoken of by him?”
sn47.21:2.2: Your intelligence is excellent, your ingenuity is excellent, your inquiry is a good one.
sn47.21:2.4: ‘Friend Ānanda, as to the wholesome virtues spoken of by the Blessed One, what is the purpose for which they were spoken of by him?’”
sn47.21:2.6: “Those wholesome virtues spoken of by the Blessed One were spoken of by him for the purpose of developing the four establishments of mindfulness.
sn47.21:3.2: Here, friend, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body …
sn47.21:3.5: phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.
sn47.21:3.6: “Those virtues spoken of by the Blessed One were spoken of by him for the sake of developing these four establishments of mindfulness.”
